meaning: 24 V dc positive feed through red spot fuse FUSE-{1} on sheet 035. Redundancy module that combines the outputs of PSU A and PSU B ('DUAL REDUNDANCY') into the 24 V dc distribution, sheet 035.

Wire number on the 230 V ac supply 'A' (N = neutral, L = live), segment {2}: NA1/LA1 at the incoming terminals, NA2/LA2 after the 20 A isolator 'A', NA3/LA3 after AC fuse 'A' (6 A) into PSU A, NA4/LA4 after AC fuse 'B' into PSU B.

meaning: Terminal group XG.{1} of the cabinet power and rack wiring (the number after the colon is the terminal within the group). Panel earth connection of the F7133 card (terminal XG.3, sheets 043-050).

Caption of the AL+, BL+ and CL+ feeds on sheet 035 (FUSE-A/B/C, 10 A): power to the HIMA PLC rack power units via terminals XG.21, XG.22, XG.23 on sheet 040.

Red spot fuse {1} in the 24 V dc L+ distribution on sheet 035, feeding circuit {1}L+ (FUSE-A, B, C 10 A 'PLC POWER'; FUSE-D 4 A 'COOLING FANS'; FUSE-1..6 4 A). Sheet 025: 'FUSE HOLDERS TO BE GEC REDSPOT, SIZE A1, FRONT CONNECTED, BLACK'.

Fuse {1} (4 A) on an F7133 24 V distribution card (sheets 043-050); its output is one nL+k wire to an I/O card position. Note 1 on 043: if F1-F4 fails the corresponding LED flashes and the card relay de-energises. (On sheet 040, F1 and F2 are the 1.6 A fuses of the Z6013 units at XG.24 / XG.25.)
LED {1} on an F7133 24 V distribution card: flashes when fuse F{1} fails; loss of the incoming 24 V dc extinguishes the LEDs (note 1, sheet 043).
Backplane link X{1} on an F7133 card sheet: it links the card fuse failure circuit to the adjacent F7133 card. Note 2 (043): 'MOVE LINK X1-X4 (CARD POSITIONS 21-18) TO POSITION 1 IF NO F7133 FITTED'.

meaning: Push-on blade connector. On the F7133 card sheets: 'FASTON CONNECTORS ON BACKPLANE' (the XG.10 / XG.1 side) and 'FASTON CONNECTORS AT FRONT OF CARD' (the nL+k / nL-k outputs to the I/O positions).

24 V dc wire {1}L{2}{3}: branch {3} of fused circuit {1}L{2}. On the L+ side it is the output of one fuse F1-F4 of an F7133 24 V distribution card, taken through a FASTON connector at the front of the card to the L+ pin of one I/O card position; on the L- side the matching return (043: 1L+1 to 1101:d30 and 1L-1 to 1101:d26; 045: 1L+9 to 1109:z12 and 1L-9 to 1109:z2). The loop drawings write the pair at the module supply ('1L+1 / 1L-1' on 075, '1L+10 / 1L-10' on 099). +ve wires are 1.0mmSq red, -ve 1.0mmSq black.

Pin {2}{3} of the I/O card connector in position {1}. The legend decodes '1112 : z6' as cabinet 1, rack 1, card position 12, pin z6; pins lie in rows z, b and d of the ELCO connector. Supply pins: d30 = L+ and d26 = L- on the F6217 analogue input card (043: 1101:d30 = 1L+1, 1101:d26 = 1L-1), z12 = L+ and z2 = L- on the F3236 digital input card (045: 1109:z12 = 1L+9, 1109:z2 = 1L-9). The ELCO schedules list the b-row pins that leave the cabinet to the annunciator and console (200: '1112:b2').

meaning: Wire number {1}/{2} = card position {1}, channel {2}. Loop drawing note 6: 'WIRE No.s ARE DEFINED USING CARD POSITION / CHANNEL NUMBER'. It is written on the wire between the field terminals and the I/O plug of the module.

I/O card position {1}{2}{3} = cabinet {1}, rack {2}, card position {3} (legend: '1112 : z6' = CABINET 1, RACK 1, CARD POSITION 12, PIN z6). Positions 1118-1121 (rack 1) and 1218-1221 (rack 2) hold the F7133 24 V distribution cards (sheets 043-050); the loop drawings give the position in the module table ('POSITION 1101 CH 1').
Range of I/O card positions {1} to {2}; on sheet 035 the feed captions '1118-1121' and '1218-1221' name the four F7133 distribution cards fed by 1L+ and 2L+.
16 channel (16-fold) testable digital input module, 24 V dc. Drawn as 'DIGITAL I/P F3236' in the INPUT column of the FLDs; typical loop DI1; I/O plug Z7116; supply pins z12 (L+) and z2 (L-).
source: 018 '16-FOLD DIGITAL INPUT MODULE'; 070 '16 CHANNEL TESTABLE DIGITAL INPUT MODULE HIMA F3236'; 045

meaning: 8 channel (8-fold) testable analogue input module, 4-20 mA. Drawn as 'ANALOG I/P F6217' in the INPUT column of the FLDs; typical loops AI1, AI2, AI3 and (through a VCON-TC converter) AI4; I/O plug Z7127; supply pins d30 (L+) and d26 (L-).
source: 018 '8-FOLD ANALOGUE INPUT MODULE'; 070 '8 CHANNEL TESTABLE ANALOGUE INPUT MODULE HIMA F6217'; 043

meaning: 8 channel (8-fold) testable 24 V dc output module. On the FLDs it drives the H4135 relay amplifier in the OUTPUT column; typical loops DO1 and DO2; I/O plug Z7138.
source: 018 '8-FOLD OUTPUT MODULE'; 071 '8 CHANNEL TESTABLE 24Vdc OUTPUT MODULE HIMA F3330'

meaning: 16 channel 24 V dc output module, non testable (typical loops DO3 and DO4): drives the annunciator windows. Note 2 on the FLDs: 'ALL ANNUNCIATOR OUTPUTS TYPICAL LOOP TYPE DO3'. I/O plug Z7136.
source: 071 '16 CHANNEL 24Vdc OUTPUT MODULE HIMA F3322'; 051 note 2

meaning: 24 V dc distribution card: takes a fused feed nL+ / nL- from sheet 035 and splits it through four 4 A fuses F1-F4 into the wires nL+k / nL-k of four I/O card positions; carries fuse evaluation logic, LEDs L1-L4 and a fuse failure relay. Cards sit in positions 1118-1121 (fed by 1L+) and 1218-1221 (fed by 2L+), sheets 043-050.

Power supply module of the HIMA PES, drawn three times as NG1/PS1, NG2/PS2 and NG3/PS3 on the main power schematic; supplies the -5V, GND and +5V rails that reach the I/O racks through XG.2 / XG.3 and XG.4 / XG.12. Monitored by the F7131 module ('POWER SUPPLY MONITORING').
source: 040 'NG1/PS1 F 7126', 'POWER SUPPLY MONITORING: NG1/PS1 NG2/PS2 NG3/PS3'

meaning: Power supply unit {1} (HIMA F 7126) of the PES on the main power schematic, sheet 040.
Module K 1412 on the main power schematic carrying 'POWER SUPPLY MONITORING: NG1/PS1, NG2/PS2, NG3/PS3' and the 'CONNECTION FOR EXTERNAL BACKUP BATTERY'.
Central module of the HIMA PES (two: ZB1/CU1 and ZB2/CU2) with the watchdog output 'WD', sheet 040.
Central unit {1} of the HIMA PES (F8650X module with watchdog WD), sheet 040.
Watchdog output of an F8650X central module, sheet 040 ('MAIN SCHEMATIC FOR POWER AND WATCHDOG').
Type of the HIMA PES (safety PLC) in the cabinet: 'B5233-1 (H51q-HS)' on the main power schematic; sheet 041 gives its communication connection details.
The HIMA programmable electronic system (H51q-HS) that runs the ESD logic. 'Programmable electronic system' is the standard expansion; the drawings write only 'HIMA PES'.
source: 031 'HIMA PES AND HSD PSU 1U LABEL STRIPS'; standard abbreviation

meaning: Relay amplifier: output relay module driven by an F3330 output channel (relays K1-3 on the typical output loop). Drawn as 'RELAY AMP H4135' in the OUTPUT column of the FLDs; its volt-free contact switches the field load (solenoid valves, 110 V ac loads).
The H4135 relay amplifier box on the FLD output side (caption line above 'H4135').

Signal converter (isolator) ISOCON-6: 1-5 V in, 4-20 mA out, powered from 24 V dc. It repeats an analogue input to the DCS and is drawn as the 'V TO I' box on the FLDs (051: 'V TO I ISOCON 6'; 075: 'SIGNAL CONVERTER ISOCON-6-20'). The number after ISOCON-6 is the unit number; the label sheet lists '13 OFF ISOCON-6'.
Signal isolator / converter VCON-HL: 1-5 V in, 4-20 mA out ('V TO I' on the FLDs); passive output powered from the DCS system (typical loop AI2, 'TESTABLE ANALOGUE NON I.S. INPUT & V/I REPEAT').
Thermocouple signal converter VCON-TC: type K thermocouple (mV) in, with cold junction compensation, 4-20 mA out to the F6217 input. Used on all loop type AI4 loops (070 note 5).
source: 070 'TESTABLE ANALOGUE NON I.S. mV/I INPUT AI4', note 5

meaning: Voltage-to-current converter box on the FLD output side: 1-5 V in, 4-20 mA out to a PROCESS DEVICE TAG (a repeat of an analogue input to the DCS). The device is an ISOCON-6 or a VCON-HL.
Caption of an ISOCON-6 / VCON-HL / VCON-TC converter on the loop drawings and typicals.
I/O plug type Z71{1}: the connector plugged into the module (Z7116 on the F3236 digital input, Z7127 on the F6217 analogue input, Z7136 on the F3322 output, Z7138 on the F3330 output).
Power distribution unit Z60{1} at the terminal groups XG.21-XG.26 on the main power schematic (Z6011 at XG.21/22/23 with a 4 A fuse, Z6013 at XG.24/25 with 1.6 A fuses F1/F2, Z6018 at XG.26).

Annunciator unit {1} of the No.3 plant annunciator (sheet 208): four units with their power supply and pushbutton inputs wired in parallel, F01-F04 linked to form one first-out group of 16, FSYNC linked so the windows flash together, common 0V for windows 01 to 48.

Delta V / Modbus reference point {2} of the No.{1} plant: a tap drawn on an FLD logic wire where that signal is passed to the Delta V system over Modbus (legend: 'REFERENCE TO DELTA V/MODBUS (AS SHOWN ON FLD DRG)'). DV3_n points are on the No.3 plant FLDs (051-056A), DV7_n on the No.7 plant FLD (057).
Delta V: the plant control system that receives ESD signals over a Modbus link. The FLD columns 'DELTA V MODBUS' hold the DVn_m reference taps; the typical loops call the same system 'DCS'.
source: 018 'REFERENCE TO DELTA V/MODBUS'; 051 headers; 'No.3 PLANT DELTA V LINK'

meaning: The plant control system (Delta V). Analogue repeat outputs are 'PASSIVE OUTPUT POWERED FROM DCS SYSTEM' (070). 'Distributed control system' is the standard expansion; the drawings do not spell it out.

The 'ICI SYNETIX ESD SYSTEM - No.3 AND No.7 PLANTS' described by this drawing set (title blocks): the HIMA PES cabinet with its field inputs, logic and outputs. 'Emergency shutdown' is the standard expansion; the drawings write only ESD.
source: title blocks; 070 'POWERED FROM THE ESD SYSTEM'; standard abbreviation

meaning: Functional Logic Diagram: sheets 051-057 ('FLD - No.3 PLANT COPPER DISSOLVING AREA' ...). The document schedule writes the full name 'FUNCTIONAL LOGIC DIAGRAM - No.3 PLANT COPPER DISSOLVING AREA'.
source: 002 document schedule; 051 title; 018 '(AS SHOWN ON FLD DRG)'

meaning: Instrument / signal tag: optional plant prefix (03 = No.3 plant, 07 = No.7 plant), function letters {1}, loop number {2}. The first letter is the measured variable or input type (F flow, L level, T temperature, P pressure, PD differential pressure, Q density, H hand-operated, E electrical / pump running, B burner, X unclassified), Z marks a safety / trip function, and the last letter the device or signal: T transmitter, S switch or contact, A alarm (software signal to an annunciator window), O output, V valve, RT repeat output. A suffix letter (A, B, C, D) distinguishes several alarm limits of one measurement; '-OVR' is the override keyswitch input of the tag. On the ELCO schedules the plant prefix is dropped and the annunciator window follows ('FZA 03002 - W01').
Plant prefix {1}: No.{1} plant (the No.3 plant FLDs 051-056A carry 03 tags, the No.7 plant FLD 057 carries 07 tags).
source: 051 title 'FLD - No.3 PLANT ...' with 03... tags; 057 'FLD - No.7 PLANT' with 07... tags

meaning: F = flow: FZT tags carry flow captions ('Recirculation Flow' 03FZT03007, 'LOW FLOW' 03FZT03002, 'Low Oxygen Flow').
L = level: 'LEVEL IN 3F3' (03LZT03691), '3F1 Dissolver Level' (03LZT03110), '3F1 MID LEVEL TRIP'.
T = temperature: 'Recirculation Temp' (03TZT03052); annunciator labels 'HIGH TEMPERATURE' for TZA tags.
PD = differential pressure: 'Vent Fan D.P.' (03PDZT03078).
P = pressure: '3F1 HIGH PRESSURE TRIP' (03PZT03079); annunciator labels 'PRESSURE TRIP'.
Q = density: 'Flow Density' (03QZT03581), 'MIXED ACID FEED DENSITY TRIP' (03QZT03581-OVR), 'NEW DENSITY METER' (051 revision E).

H = hand-operated: HZS tags are the control room pushbuttons ('LOW FLOWS RESET' 03HZS03350, 'COPPER DISSOLVING STOP' 03HZS03354) and HZA the keyswitch 'NORMAL OPERATION/OVERRIDE' (03HZA03559), drawn with the P/B and K/S symbols.
E: drawn on electrical drive signals: '3J4A Pump Running' / '3J4B Pump Running' (03EZS03412 / 03EZS03413, digital inputs) and the 110 V ac outputs 03EZO03403A. ISA 5.1 reads E as voltage.
B = burner: 07BZS07200 sits next to the 'BURNER - NORMAL OVERRIDE' keyswitch and the 'BURNER TRIP' window on the No.7 plant drawings.
XZV tags are shut-off and dump valves: 'GAS SHUT-OFF VALVE' (03XZV03853), 'MIXED ACID VALVE' (03XZV03591), 'F61 DUMP VALVE' (03XZV03742). ISA 5.1 leaves X unclassified.
Y: no caption on the drawings explains it (03YS03228 / 03YS03229 are digital inputs on sheet 054, windows 'YSA 03228'). ISA 5.1 reads Y as event, state or presence.
G: no caption on the drawings explains it (03GZS03568 is a digital input on sheet 054). ISA 5.1 reads G as gauging or position.

Z = safety / trip function: nearly every tag of this ESD system carries a Z, and the captions read 'TRIP' ('3F1 HIGH PRESSURE TRIP', '3F1 MID LEVEL TRIP', 'DENSITY TRIP OVERRIDE'). ISA 5.1 reads Z as a safety instrumented function.
T (last letter) = transmitter: the field device of an analogue input loop, drawn 'Tx' on the typical loops and in the FIELD column oval on the FLDs (03FZT03002 'Nitric Acid').

RT = repeat output: the 4-20 mA copy of a measurement sent from a 'V TO I' converter to the PROCESS DEVICE TAG column of the FLD (03FZRT03007 repeats 03FZT03007; typical loop AI2 'INPUT & V/I REPEAT'). ISA 5.1 would read R as record.
source: 051 OUTPUT / PROCESS DEVICE TAG columns; 070 'V/I REPEAT'; ISA 5.1 convention

meaning: S (last letter) = switch or contact: HZS pushbuttons and keyswitches, EZS pump running contacts, PZS pressure switches; all are digital inputs (F3236).
SH: switch, high limit. Not captioned on the drawings (03PZSH tags); ISA 5.1 convention.
A (last letter) = alarm: the software signal derived from a measurement on the FLD logic side (03FZA03002 from 03FZT03002), carried to an annunciator window (ELCO schedule 'FZA 03002 - W01').

O (last letter) = output: ZO, EZO and TZO tags sit in the OUTPUT column of the FLDs, driven by an F3330 output module through an H4135 relay amplifier; captions name solenoid valves ('NITRIC ACID S0V', '50V DC') or 110 V ac loads ('BMS'). Read from the drawing position; not an ISA 5.1 letter meaning.
V (last letter) = valve: 'GAS SHUT-OFF VALVE' 03XZV03853, 'F61 DUMP VALVE' 03XZV03742.

Suffix {1}: one of several alarm limits derived from the same measurement; the limit word is written on the FLD logic wire (051: 03TZA03052A HIGH, 03TZA03052B LOW, 03TZA03052C HIHI, 03TZA03052D LOLO; 03LZA03110A HIGH, 03LZA03110C MID).

-OVR = override: the keyswitch input that overrides the tag's trip, drawn on the loop drawings as a keyswitch '(KS)' into an F3236 digital input ('03FZT03002-OVR 69% NITRIC ACID LOW FLOW OVERRIDE (KS)'). The FLD INPUT column has an 'O/R' sub-column for these.
ELCO schedule entry: the alarm tag written before the dash drives annunciator window {1}; the row gives the cable terminal and pin and the ESD cabinet connector pin it leaves on.

Annunciator window {1}{2}. The ELCO schedules (200-206) list the alarm tag that drives each window ('FZA 03002 - W01') and its cable terminal; the FLDs draw the window as a status indication lamp in the ANNUN/CONSOLE column; sheets 026/027 give the window label text; sheets 208/209 wire the annunciator units (windows 01-48 in four OMNI units, first-out groups of 16).
source: 018 'STATUS INDICATION LAMP'; 200; 026 'No.3 PLANT ANNUNCIATOR WINDOW LABEL DETAILS'; 208 note 5

meaning: Unused window or connector position on the ELCO schedules.

Field cable C{2} of the No.{1} plant: the prefix is the plant number (3/C655-1 is the 'No.3 PLANT ANNUN SUPPLY', 7/C305-1 the 'No.7 PLANT ANNUN SUPPLY' on sheet 035). A trailing /n is a core number (3/C735/1), -n one cable of a pair (3/C655-1 / -2). On the FLDs the cores used by a loop are written under the cable number in the CABLE & TERMINALS column ('1 & 2'). The ELCO schedules name the multicore cables to the annunciator and console as 'VARELCO BLOCK 3/C652' (18 core x 0.5, black).
Cores {1} and {2} of the cable written above (FLD CABLE & TERMINALS column); on the loop drawings the same pair appears as the field terminal numbers of the loop.

Multi-pin rectangular connector block. The I/O modules plug into ELCO connectors (pins in rows z, b, d; legend symbols for the female and male halves); the multicore cables to the annunciator and operator console land on VARELCO blocks named after their cable ('VARELCO BLOCK 3/C652'). Sheet 200 gives the polarising code ('R-G-4-S-3': insulator body type, guide pin / socket, positions 1 through 6).
The VARELCO connector block on which multicore cable {1} terminates; the ELCO schedule beside it lists TERM, PIN, core colour and the signal on each way.

Terminal block on the cabinet backplate (sheet 022) for the No.{1} plant: AI = analogue inputs, DI = digital inputs, DO = digital outputs (the I/O type words come from the typical loop headings AI/DI/DO). /n is the terminal number on the block (loop drawings 092-097 'TB3DI/4'). 'TB3D0' with a zero on sheets 119-122 is the same block TB3DO.
Typical loop AI1 'TESTABLE ANALOGUE NON I.S. INPUT' (sheet 070): a 4-20 mA transmitter (Tx) on an F6217 channel, 2 wire with single core screen; passive transmitters are powered from the ESD system.

Typical loop AI2 'TESTABLE ANALOGUE NON I.S. INPUT & V/I REPEAT' (sheet 070): as AI1 plus a VCON-HL converter that repeats the 1-5 V signal as 4-20 mA to the DCS (passive output powered from the DCS system). On the FLDs the repeat appears as a 'V TO I' box feeding a ...RT process device tag.

Typical loop AI3 'TESTABLE ANALOGUE NON I.S. INPUT & V/I REPEAT' for active transmitters powered from the field device (sheet 070, right-hand typical): 2 core cable with overall screen, F6217 channel, VCON-HL repeat.
Typical loop AI4 'TESTABLE ANALOGUE NON I.S. mV/I INPUT' (sheet 070): a type K thermocouple (T/C) through a VCON-TC signal converter with cold junction compensation into an F6217 channel (note 5).

Typical loop DI1 'TESTABLE DIGITAL NON I.S. INPUT - 24Vdc' (sheet 070): a volt-free field contact, L+ out and signal back in 0.5mmSq grey, into an F3236 channel (I/O plug Z7116). Used for pushbuttons, keyswitches and pump running contacts.
Typical loop DO1 'TESTABLE DIGITAL NON I.S. OUTPUT - VFC VIA RELAY' (sheet 071): an F3330 output channel drives an H4135 relay amplifier whose volt-free contact switches the field load (< 4 A).

Typical loop DO2 'TESTABLE DIGITAL NON I.S. OUTPUT - VFC VIA RELAY' (sheet 071, lower typical): as DO1 with the contact wired to 24 V dc wires 1L+12 / 1L-12. The FLDs use DO2 for the ZO / EZO outputs (solenoid valves, sheet 052 '50V DC'; note 2 on 071: 50 V supply for solenoid valve outputs by others).

Typical loop DO3 'NON TESTABLE DIGITAL OUTPUT' (sheet 071): an F3322 16 channel 24 V dc output module drives a remote annunciator window (< 12 W; L- from the 24 V dc supply via a 2 core cable). FLD note 2: 'ALL ANNUNCIATOR OUTPUTS TYPICAL LOOP TYPE DO3'.
Typical loop DO4 'NON TESTABLE DIGITAL OUTPUT' (sheet 071): an F3322 output to a front of panel (F.O.P.) annunciator.
FLD note 1: the loop wiring of every input and output is drawn once per loop type on the typical sheets 070 (inputs) and 071 (outputs).

Override: the INPUT sub-column of the FLDs that holds override inputs. The override keyswitch loops are drawn on the loop drawings as '<tag>-OVR ... OVERRIDE (KS)' into F3236 digital inputs (sheet 099).

Non-intrinsically-safe circuit (standard abbreviation; the drawings do not spell 'intrinsically safe' out). The legend's wire colour table separates IS and NON IS wiring: NON IS DIGITAL = GREY 0.5mmSq, NON IS ANALOG = screened cable. All typical loops in this set are 'NON I.S.'; the ELCO schedules are 'NON I.S. - ESD TO ANNUNCIATOR SIGNALS'.

Intrinsically safe (standard abbreviation, not spelled out on the drawings): IS DIGITAL = BLUE 0.5mmSq, IS ANALOG = screened cable, I.S. EARTH = GREEN/BLUE BAND (legend). The FLD OUTPUT column has an I.S. sub-column; it is empty on sheet 051.
Pushbutton (legend: 'PUSHBUTTON (AS SHOWN ON FLD DRG)'). On the FLDs the symbol carries a letter (C, F, B) and the caption 'CONTROL ROOM'.
Keyswitch (legend: 'KEYSWITCH (AS SHOWN ON FLD DRG)'). '(KS)' after an override caption on the loop drawings marks the override keyswitch.
Location caption under the pushbutton and keyswitch symbols on the FLDs: the device is in the control room.
Alarm / trip limit of the software signal on the FLD logic wire it is written on: {1}.
Timer T{1}, {2} delay; the time is written below ('2 mins', '3-30 MINS'). Legend: 'TIMER (AS SHOWN ON FLD DRG)'.
Logic gate on the FLD: inputs enter on the left edge, the output leaves on the right (legend: "'AND' GATE", "'OR' GATE").
Module box in the FLD INPUT column: '{1} I/P' over the module type (ANALOG I/P F6217, DIGITAL I/P F3236). Field side on the left, software signal on the right.
Single core screen: the screen of the analogue loop cable, landed at the module side of the loop (loop drawings and typical 070).
Screen connection of the loop cable at the module supply pins (loop drawings).
Overall screen of a 2 core cable (typical loops AI3 / AI4, sheet 070).
Transmitter: the field device of an analogue input loop on the typical sheet 070.
Thermocouple (type K) field device of loop type AI4, sheet 070.
Input / output plug: the connector (Z7116, Z7127, Z7136, Z7138) that carries the field wiring into the module.

Heading of the module table on the loop drawings: PIN = module pin(s) of the channel, POSITION = card position, CH = channel number, PINS = supply pins of the module (d26 L- / d30 L+ on the F6217, z2 L- / z12 L+ on the F3236).
Signal or supply level of the connection it is written on: 1-5 V converter input, 4-20 mA loop current, 24 V dc supply, 50 V dc / 110 V ac output load supply.

Conductor size {1} mm2 (and colour {2}) of the wire it is written beside. Legend: 24 V +ve red, 24 V -ve black, logic grey 0.5mmSq, IS digital blue, 120 V live brown / neutral blue / earth yellow-green.
Tri-rated cable; legend: 'ALL WIRING TO BE TRI-RATED BS6231'.

The conductor is run as a closed ring fed from both ends: the 24 V dc L+ bus (6.0mmSq red) and L- bus (6.0mmSq black) on sheet 035; sheet 040: '+5v, GND & L- WIRING TO THE BACK OF THE I/O RACKS IS TO BE WIRED AS RING'.
Solenoid operated valve (standard abbreviation): the ZO output captions on sheet 052 read 'NITRIC ACID S0V', 'SCRUB LIQUOR S0V', 'MIXED ACID S0V', 'OXYGEN S0V' with '50V DC'.
Burner management system (standard abbreviation): destination of the 110 V ac outputs 07TZO07044 / 07TZO07048 on the No.7 plant FLD.
Volt-free contact (standard abbreviation): typical loop headings 'DIGITAL NON I.S. OUTPUT - VFC VIA RELAY'.
Front of panel annunciator (071 note 3: 'L- FOR REMOTE AND FRONT OF PANEL ANNUNCIATORS IS DERIVED FROM THE 24Vdc SUPPLY'); loop type DO4.
ASK1 fuse terminal (legend symbol). Loop drawing note 1: the first terminal of a pair is always '+' and is an ASK1 (50 mA) fuse terminal on analogue inputs only.
SAKR link terminal (legend symbol: a terminal with a disconnect link).
The small circle symbol on the FLDs and power sheets is a terminal (legend); a slash through it marks a link or disconnect terminal.
Lamp test pushbutton input of the annunciator units (208: VARELCO 3/C656 terminal 17 'LAMP TEST PUSHBUTTON').
Circuit test pushbutton input of the annunciator units (208: VARELCO 3/C656 terminal 16 'CIRCUIT TEST PUSHBUTTON').
Acknowledge pushbutton input of the annunciator units (208: terminal 14 'ACKNOWLEDGE PUSHBUTTON').
Reset pushbutton input of the annunciator units (208: terminal 15 'RESET PUSHBUTTON').
Silence pushbutton input of the annunciator units (208: terminal 13 'SILENCE PUSHBUTTON').
Common 0 V of the annunciator pushbutton circuit (208: terminal 18) and of the window inputs 01 to 48, wired as a ring (note 5).
Annunciator unit terminal 'INH' (sheet 208); the drawing does not expand it (standard reading: inhibit).
Flash synchronisation link between the annunciator units: note 4 on 208, 'FSYNC TO BE WIRED TOGETHER TO ENABLE THE ALARM WINDOWS TO FLASH IN SYNCHRONIZATION'.
First-out group link of the annunciator units: note 3 on 208, 'F01, F02, F03 & F04 TO BE WIRED TOGETHER TO FORM ONE FIRST OUT GROUP OF 16'.
Watchdog terminal of the annunciator unit (sheet 208, not wired on the drawing).
Relay contact output of each annunciator unit with terminals N.C., N.O. and C (sheet 208). The drawing does not expand 'G.A.' (standard reading: group alarm).
Horn output of the annunciator unit (+24V, O.C., 0V) driving the sounder on 'TERM BLOCK AUDIABLE' (sheet 208).
Horn output terminal 'O.C.' of the annunciator unit (sheet 208); not expanded on the drawing (standard reading: open collector).
Contact wetting supply of the annunciator unit: 'I/P +24V' and 'I/P 0V' terminals (sheet 208).
Normally closed contact (legend 'N.C. CONTACT').
Normally open contact (legend 'N.O. CONTACT').
Terminal block in the annunciator cabinet: 'TERM BLOCK 3/C655' receives the 24 V dc annunciator supply (+VE, -VE, EARTH), 'TERM BLOCK AUDIABLE' feeds the sounder (sheet 208).

Row heading of an ELCO schedule: TERM = terminal number of the VARELCO block, PIN = pin letter, CONTROLS = the alarm tag and window on the annunciator / console side, ESD = the ESD cabinet connector pin (1112:b2).
The multicore cable between the ESD cabinet and the annunciator / console VARELCO blocks (200: 'INTERCONNECTING CABLE COLOUR BLACK SIZE 18 Core x 0.5 LENGTH 20/50 METRES').

ELCO connector polarising code, e.g. 'R-G-4-S-3': insulator body type (R male, P female), location side large diameter (G guide pin, S guide socket) and position 1-6, location side small diameter and position; the example 'R-G-4-S-3' mates with 'P-S-4-G-3' (sheet 200).
Maker of the PES and I/O modules ('HIMA F6217', 'HIMA PES'); the drawings are by HIMA-SELLA LIMITED.
The 24 V dc 0 V bus of sheet 035 ('24Vdc DISTRIBUTION FOR L- SAFECLIP LINKS'), referenced from the rack wiring on sheet 040.

A lettered box ('AA') on an FLD logic wire with the destination written beside it as drawing serial number . grid reference ('03.212'); the destination sheet carries the same letter box with a pointer back. The FLD signal letters (3A, 3P ...) are these boxes.
